messages:
alex: kicking off verification for the new cedar-region GPU cluster. goal: smoke + capacity + network + cost guards. handing off to oncall when green.
priya: thanks — can you paste the minimal smoke checklist here so oncall can follow?
alex: short checklist below, will run now and paste outputs.

alex: SMOKE CHECKLIST (minimal):
- control-plane health: api-server, scheduler, node-controller
- kubelet on all GPU nodes reporting Ready and correct labels (gpu=true, zone=cedar-a/b)
- kernel drivers + nvidia-smi present on all nodes
- pod network connectivity across AZs (ping + curl to metadata)
- block storage mount + write test for model volumes
- basic inference job: pull model, serve small batch, measure p95 latency < 120ms
- autoscaler synthesize scale-up/down and validate cooldowns
- cost guard: per-node preemptible/spot rate, burst cap configured

mike: running node checks now:
```
# parallel ssh check nvidia
for n in $(cat nodes.txt); do ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv"; done
```

alex: infra-bot: run quick-control-plane-health for cedar-region please

infra-bot: control-plane status: api-server=ok, etcd=ok, controller-manager=ok, scheduler=ok (checked at 2345678980) :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: 24/24 gpu nodes Ready, 2 nodes in cedara with taints=none, labels ok

priya: network checks next. mike can you validate cross-AZ ping and MTU? last time MTU mismatch killed large tensor transfers.
mike: running ping and iperf tests, and checking routes + egress. expected MTU=8900

mike: iperf output:
```
[  5]  0.0-10.0 sec  9.3 GBytes  8.02 Gbits/sec
MTU verified 8900 on all nodes
Route check: VPC peering to central VPC has allowed-ranges configured for 10.10.0.0/16
BGP sessions to provider1 established
```

tara: good. add a step to validate host route propagation to edge proxies and verify connection to logging endpoint (elasticsearch) with TLS.

alex: logging check: curl -vk https://logs.cedar.redwood.internal/health -> 200, cert sha256 matches prod pinned hash

priya: storage test: created a 100GB model volume on gp2-class, mounted on /models, wrote 5GB test file, fsync ok.

mike: inference smoke job deployed: image: rwd-infer:test-smoke, replicas=3, batch=4
Test results: 500 requests, p50=45ms, p95=110ms, errors=0

alex: autoscaler test: simulated load up to 150% target qps, autoscaler scaled from 3 -> 10 nodes within 90s, scale-down back to 3 after cooldown 300s. no stuck terminating nodes.

infra-bot: cost-guard check: burst-cap configured = 12 nodes, reserved-capacity commit = 8 nodes, spot-fallback policy enabled

billing-bot: estimated incremental monthly cost at current config ~ $28k (gpu hours + egress). Alerting thresholds set at +20% over baseline.

tara: SLO gates: latency p95 < 150ms, error rate < 0.5%, availability (control plane + nodes) > 99.9% for initial ramp. confirm these are in the console.
priya: added SLOs to console, created dashboard with token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency.

alex: remaining manual checks:
- security groups: only mgmt IPs allowed to SSH, kube API restricted to control plane CIDR
- KMS key access verified for model volumes
- audit logs flowing to central audit bucket (check last 24h)
- canary traffic test: route 1% of prod requests to cedar_region canary endpoint

mike: SSH rule confirmed. KMS policy allowed for infra-service-account. audit logs uploaded, last event 2345678999.

priya: canary test: deployed canary proxy, 1% traffic diverted, requests served successfully for 2k requests, latency stable.

alex: checklist green. tagging for handoff. @sre-oncall can you take ownership of the region for 72h ramp monitoring? include runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/cedar-region-ga (runbook has full steps)

sre-oncall: taking it. will run rolling restart test, verify fallback policies and watch alerts. assign oncall rotation to tara for first 12h.

tara: on it. will keep a close eye on cost spikes and network flaps. please put escalation path in thread.

alex: escalation: pager->sre-oncall, slack #eng-sre, if network-related -> infra-net escalation policy page, for cost -> @finance-pmo.

infra-bot: recorded summary: smoke pass, autoscaler pass, network MTU ok, storage ok, canary pass.

billing-bot: created cost alert in billing console: threshold = baseline * 1.2, notify channels = #eng-finance, @tara, @sre-oncall

priya: final ask: add a short-living quota cap to prevent runaway during initial ramp: set node quota = 20 for cedar-region for next 48h.
mike: quota applied.

alex: thanks all — handing off to @sre-oncall and closing this thread for ops. will update runbook with any post-mortem notes. :thumbsup:
